question: Concerns have arisen over Commissioner Virkkunen’s neutrality in the round table talks to discuss media freedom ahead of the 2025 Polish presidential elections. This is due to the Commissioner’s previous political support for Warsaw Mayor Rafał Trzaskowski, as evidenced by her tweets supporting Mr Trzaskowski in his election campaign in 2020.

This previous political partisanship demonstrates that the meeting may be seen as political interference from the Commission in the upcoming election, favouring the candidate from the Warsaw Mayor’s party. Statements and actions by Commission members have previously been seen as attempts to influence elections in EU states.

Examples include comments before elections in Italy and post-election pressure on Romania regarding judicial matters. These instances raise concerns that the Commission’s involvement in Poland’s pre-election talks could be viewed as political interference rather than a neutral effort to uphold democratic standards. Therefore, we ask the Commission the following questions: 1.
Does the Commission have specific guidelines to avoid conflicts of interest and ensure neutrality in Commissioners’ work?

Will the Commission commit to full transparency by publishing transcripts of the meetings between Commissioner Virkkunen and Mayor Trzaskowski to refute any possible claims of interference in the presidential election?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (26.6.

2025) Conflicts of interests involving Members of the Commission are dealt within the framework of the Code of Conduct for the Members of the European Commission1, which details the ethical rules applicable to Members of the Commission enshrined in the relevant articles on the Treaties, namely Article 17(3) of the Treaty on European Union and Article 245 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union.

However, the participation of a Commissioner in a political debate is not covered by the definition of conflict of interest in Article 2(6) of the Code of Conduct, which reads: ‘A conflict of interest arises where a personal interest may influence the independent performance of their duties.

Personal interests include, but are not limited to, any potential benefit or advantage to Members themselves, their spouses, partners or direct family members. A conflict of interest does not exist where a Member is only concerned as a member of the general public or of a broad class of persons.

’ The Commission publishes information on meetings held by Members of the College with, among others, representatives of public authorities or political parties of the Member States on their online public calendars or through other channels of communication.

Additionally, the Commission publishes information on all meetings as well as the minutes of the meetings held by Members of the College and their Cabinets with interest representatives in accordance with Commission Decision (EU) 2024/30812. Meetings with representatives of public authorities or political parties as well as meetings of a purely private or social character are excluded from this Decision.
